threats.title: Spoofed pre-authentication access signalling
threats.description: A local transmitter imitates access signalling before a protected session is established. The candidate concerns disruption of attachment. Successful impersonation after mutual authentication is not claimed.
threats.actor: External actor with suitable transmitting equipment and protocol knowledge.
threats.conditions: Radio proximity and a suitable transmitter plus an assumed pre-authentication handling weakness. The weakness has not been demonstrated for a selected NR implementation.
threats.controls: Primary authentication and applicable signalling integrity are assumed effective after security activation. The proposed threat is limited to the earlier access stage.
threats.consequence: The assumed effect is repeated attachment disruption for nearby users of the shared service. Subscriber keys and protected sessions are not assumed compromised.
threats.feasibility_reason: F2 is a conditional estimate because specialist radio access and an unconfirmed pre-authentication weakness are required. It is not evidence of a practical bypass.
threats.impact_reason: I3 assumes several nearby users of the shared service experience attachment disruption. If only one UE is affected then this score must be reduced.
threats.confidence_reason: Low confidence in the scenario-specific attack and ratings. Normative control support is separate from deployment evidence. No S1 system or incident data was inspected.

evidence.locator: v18.5.0 clause 5.1.2; printed p.30 / PDF p.31; clause 5.3.3; printed p.33 / PDF p.34
evidence.note: Authentication and signalling-protection context. The source does not establish the hypothesized pre-authentication exploit. Assistant-assisted source preparation dated 17 October 2026. Student source check is still pending.
The selected pre-authentication weakness and the several-user effect are hypotheses for review. Reject or leave unscored if neither student can justify this conditional path.

mitigations.text: Apply primary authentication and the required signalling integrity checks. Review handling of unprotected access messages.
mitigations.note: Clauses 5.1.2 and 5.3.3. The standard supports authentication and integrity controls. It does not say that every access request is digitally signed. Exact pre-authentication mitigation remains implementation-dependent.

threats.title: NTN gateway tampering
threats.description: An insider or attacker with write-capable ground administration access changes gateway or gNB configuration through F5. The altered configuration affects the ground transport service.
threats.actor: Insider or attacker with gateway management access.
threats.conditions: Write-capable management access and missing or bypassed change approval or integrity checking.
threats.controls: Account authentication and recoverable configuration backups are assumed. The write workflow is assumed not to require independent approval. These are model assumptions.
threats.consequence: Unauthorized changes compromise the selected ground administration configuration.
threats.feasibility_reason: F2 because a restricted management position or privileged account plus a plausible control weakness is required.
threats.impact_reason: I4 because the defined consequence is compromise of ground administration. This directly matches the severe-impact criterion.
threats.confidence_reason: Low confidence in the scenario-specific attack and ratings. Normative control support is separate from deployment evidence. No S1 system or incident data was inspected.

evidence.locator: v18.5.0 clause 5.3.4; printed p.34 / PDF p.35
evidence.note: Direct requirement context for authenticated and authorized gNB configuration. Applying an equivalent control to the modeled gateway is a project design choice. Assistant-assisted source preparation dated 17 October 2026. Student source check is still pending.

evidence.locator: Release 5.2.0 control IDs CM-3 and CM-5 plus SI-7
evidence.note: General support for change governance and integrity monitoring. These controls do not prove that this gateway is vulnerable. Assistant-assisted source preparation dated 17 October 2026. Student source check is still pending.
The actual gateway management software and its approval workflow are not known. Authorized configuration integrity can fail under the stated scenario.

mitigations.text: Require approved changes and restrict configuration writes. Compare critical configuration against an authorized baseline and retain change records.
mitigations.note: CM-3; CM-5; SI-7. The previous TPM-specific proposal is withdrawn because its support and platform design were not established. Generic integrity checking is not a claim that a TPM checks arbitrary runtime gateway configuration.

mitigations.text: Authenticate and authorize gNB management changes and protect the O&M channel.
mitigations.note: Clause 5.3.4; printed p.34 / PDF p.35. The normative requirement applies to C4. Extension to C3 is a stated S1 control proposal.

threats.title: Satellite relay eavesdropping
threats.description: A passive receiver in the footprint observes radio traffic. The record concerns metadata rather than decryption of ciphertext.
threats.actor: Passive receiver in the satellite footprint.
threats.conditions: Radio access and specialist receiving capability for the selected signal. No decryption key is assumed available.
threats.consequence: Limited metadata exposure. Ciphertext is not assumed to be decrypted.
threats.feasibility_reason: F2 is proposed because the selected NR signal and suitable receiver are unspecified. The maritime DVB-S2 equipment result is not enough to justify a commodity NR receiver claim.
threats.impact_reason: I2 for limited visible traffic-pattern metadata under the assumed active ciphering. No plaintext recovery is assumed.
threats.confidence_reason: Low confidence in the scenario-specific attack and ratings. Normative control support is separate from deployment evidence. No S1 system or incident data was inspected.

threats.title: 5G Core interface DoS
threats.description: An attacker floods signalling or user traffic towards the selected core path.
threats.actor: Attacker with a path towards the core interfaces.
threats.conditions: Access to an accepted core-facing traffic path and an assumed policing or capacity weakness. Unauthenticated traffic is not assumed able to bypass every interface control.
threats.controls: Peer protection and partial traffic policing are assumed. The candidate asks what happens when admitted traffic exceeds the selected service capacity.
threats.consequence: Disruption affecting several users of the shared service.
threats.feasibility_reason: F2 because the actor needs a privileged or otherwise accepted route into the selected core-facing path plus a policing weakness.
threats.impact_reason: I3 assumes temporary degradation for several users sharing S1. It does not claim sustained operator-wide failure.
threats.confidence_reason: Low confidence in the scenario-specific attack and ratings. Normative control support is separate from deployment evidence. No S1 system or incident data was inspected.

threats.title: Administration repudiation
threats.description: A privileged operator denies changes or removes selected local administration records. The modeled consequence is a limited audit gap that temporarily disrupts change verification.
threats.actor: Administrator or attacker with stolen administration credentials.
threats.conditions: Permission to affect local audit records and no independently protected copy for the selected change period. The local C6 history represents changes to C3 and C4.
threats.controls: Only local administration logs are assumed.
threats.consequence: Temporary disruption of administrative investigation and change verification. Service loss and disclosure of sensitive configuration are not established by log loss alone.
threats.feasibility_reason: F2 because privileged access to the relevant local records is required.
threats.impact_reason: I2 is proposed for the explicitly limited and temporary disruption of administration work. The old I3 reason did not establish several-user service loss or sensitive-data exposure.
threats.confidence_reason: Low confidence in the scenario-specific attack and ratings. Normative control support is separate from deployment evidence. No S1 system or incident data was inspected.

evidence.locator: Release 5.2.0 control IDs AU-9; AU-9(2); AU-9(3); AU-10; AU-12
evidence.note: Supports protecting action evidence and placing protected records outside the affected component. It does not quantify the S1 consequence. Assistant-assisted source preparation dated 17 October 2026. Student source check is still pending.
Only the selected local change-history interval is affected. Temporary administrative disruption is the consequence used for I2. Reassess if broader irreversible loss is part of the agreed scenario.

mitigations.text: Keep protected remote audit copies with integrity protection and limit who can alter logging. Record attributable administrative actions.
mitigations.note: AU-9; AU-9(2); AU-9(3); AU-10; AU-12. An append-only implementation or signed records may realize these aims. Neither was implemented or tested in the selected NTN system.

threats.title: Jamming of the service radio link
threats.description: Interference on the service radio link may disrupt the selected shared access service.
threats.actor: Attacker with access to the relevant radio environment.
threats.conditions: Suitable interference equipment and a suitable location.
threats.controls: Protocol authentication and payload ciphering are assumed. No validated anti-jam waveform or diverse access path is assumed.
threats.consequence: The plan assumes disruption for several users sharing the affected service.
threats.feasibility_reason: F2 because suitable interference equipment and access to the relevant local radio environment are required. Power and range are not estimated.
threats.impact_reason: I3 assumes several nearby users sharing the affected service experience temporary radio-access disruption. A one-UE-only effect would justify a lower impact.
threats.confidence_reason: Low confidence in the scenario-specific attack and ratings. Normative control support is separate from deployment evidence. No S1 system or incident data was inspected.

evidence.note: Identifies hostile wireless signal interference as a control concern. It does not quantify feasibility for this LEO radio profile. Assistant-assisted source preparation dated 17 October 2026. Student source check is still pending.
